annotations.annotation_text: Page 607 opens Book 4, Chapter 1 ("The Ricorso — Dawn") during the Ricorso (The Return) phase. This passage continues dawn breaking over Dublin Bay, St. Kevin bathing at Glendalough, St. Patrick vs. the Archdruid Balkelly, ALP's dissolving final monologue into the sea, featuring St. Kevin, St. Patrick, Balkelly, ALP. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 607 ("The Ricorso — Dawn"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Ricorso (The Return) dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.

annotations.annotation_text: Tavern/jury motif "Bar" on page 607 ("The Ricorso — Dawn"): the twelve customers drinking in HCE's Chapelizod pub represent public opinion, the Zodiac, and the Apostles within dawn breaking over Dublin Bay, St. Kevin bathing at Glendalough, St. Patrick vs. the Archdruid Balkelly, ALP's dissolving final monologue into the sea. During this Ricorso (The Return) phase, they judge, condemn, and demand another round — the Greek chorus of middle-class Dublin gossip.
